messages.text: Caballo De Mar upsets Scandinavia in Cadran clash

metadata.summary: Caballo De Mar brought an end to Scandinavia’s eight-race winning run when repeating his win in the Qatar Prix du Cadran from 12 months ago in a thrilling finish at ParisLongchamp.
metadata.content: ParisLongchamp: Caballo De Mar upsets Scandinavia in Prix du Cadran | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content ParisLongchamp: Caballo De Mar upsets Scandinavia in Prix du Cadran After surviving a lengthy stewards' enquiry, Caballo De Mar retained his Prix du Cadran crown, defeating red-hot favourite Scandinavia in a thrilling renewal of the Group 1 staying contest at ParisLongchamp. Saturday 3 October 2026 17:07, UK Image: Caballo De Mar - back-to-back winner of the Prix du Cadran Caballo De Mar brought an end to Scandinavia’s eight-race winning run when repeating his win in the Qatar Prix du Cadran from 12 months ago in a thrilling finish at ParisLongchamp. George Scott's stayer was delivered by Oisin Murphy at the furlong marker to grab the lead from Scandinavia and the fading pacesetter Queenstown. As the pair locked horns through the final furlong, Scandinavia regained the lead only for Caballo De Mar to fight back in the shadow of the post to get up by a neck. Connections had to sweat through a stewards' inquiry after an objection by Ryan Moore, whose mount Scandinavia, the 1-6 favourite, appeared to receive a bump from the 9-2 winner close to the finish. messages.text: Hamilton hopes for 'awesome' Verstappen fight for win

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton says it will be important for Ferrari to focus on their own race for what is expected to be a challenging Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia but admits it would be "awesome" if they have the pace to stay with polesitter Max Verstappen from the front row.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver hopes he can battle Max Verstappen for Bahrain GP in Malaysia win after F1 qualifying front-row | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver hopes he can battle Max Verstappen for Bahrain GP in Malaysia win after F1 qualifying front-row Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton to start on a Grand Prix front row together for the first time since 2023; Drivers expecting challenging conditions with high tyre wear; watch the race at 8am on Sunday with build-up from 6.30am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Saturday 3 October 2026 18:04, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton's wholesome reaction to qualifying on front row at Bahrain GP in Malaysia Lewis Hamilton says it will be important for Ferrari to focus on their own race for what is expected to be a challenging Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia but admits it would be "awesome" if they have the pace to stay with polesitter Max Verstappen from the front row. ​Hamilton produced "probably my best lap of the year" to claim second on the grid with his last attempt of qualifying at the Sepang International Circuit, his second front-row start of the year. It will be the first time Verstappen and Hamilton, the grid's two-most successful drivers and the sport's biggest names, have started at the head of a Grand Prix together since July 2023, at that year's Hungarian Grand Prix. messages.text: Fairy Glen foils Sunly in Prix de Royallieu

metadata.summary: Fairy Glen came from last to first in the Qatar Prix de Royallieu to floor odds-on favourite Sunly and land a Group One prize for Newmarket training duo Simon and Ed Crisford.
metadata.content: ParisLongchamp: Crisford-trained Fairy Glen foils Sunly in Prix de Royallieu | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content ParisLongchamp: Crisford-trained Fairy Glen foils Sunly in Prix de Royallieu Simon and Ed Crisford's Fairy Glen chased down Sunly to win the 2026 Prix de Royallieu on day one of Arc weekend at ParisLongchamp; Also on the day, the George Scott-trained Wimbledon Hawkeye struck gold in the Prix Dollar. Saturday 3 October 2026 16:09, UK Image: Ed and Simon Crisford trained Fairy Glen to Group 1 glory Fairy Glen came from last to first in the Qatar Prix de Royallieu to floor odds-on favourite Sunly and land a Group One prize for Newmarket training duo Simon and Ed Crisford. Anchored in last place by Mickael Barzalona as Consent, Cameo, Sugar Island and Amelia Earhart cut out a decent pace in the one-mile-six-furlong contest, the five-year-old delivered a withering challenge up the straight. Sunly, who was backed into favouritism at 5-6, had taken up the running a furlong from home, but with a target to aim at Barzalona and Fairy Glen came late and wide to grab top spot by a neck. St Leger third Amelia Earhart battled on well to hold third place, another three-quarters of a length back. messages.text: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

metadata.summary: Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.
metadata.content: Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture By Anthony Joseph and Andy Gales Saturday 3 October 2026 17:25, UK Image: Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson had his pre-match press conference cut short Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media. The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday. The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli. An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter. messages.text: 'Three tenths backwards' - Wolff admits confusion over Mercedes upgrades

metadata.summary: Toto Wolff has admitted his surprise at Mercedes' major upgrade package for the Bahrain Grand Prix having appeared to take the team backwards, following an underwhelming qualifying display.
metadata.content: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admits confusion over lack of qualifying pace following upgrades at Bahrain GP in Malaysia | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Mercedes boss Toto Wolff admits confusion over lack of qualifying pace following upgrades at Bahrain GP in Malaysia Mercedes endured a disappointing qualifying display in their upgraded car as Kimi Antonelli was fourth and George Russell eighth; Max Verstappen took pole ahead of Lewis Hamilton; watch the race at 8am with build-up from 6.30am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event Saturday 3 October 2026 13:08, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of qualifying at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on the Sepang International Circuit Toto Wolff has admitted his surprise at Mercedes' major upgrade package for the Bahrain Grand Prix having appeared to take the team backwards, following an underwhelming qualifying display. Despite dominating the 2026 season, Mercedes have brought far fewer upgrades than their rivals at the front of the grid, which meant anticipation had built around the addition of their first major package since May. The Silver Arrows arrived in Malaysia, which is hosting the event due to ongoing conflict in the Middle East, off the back of three successive race victories, and most expected that streak to continue with the help of the upgrades. messages.text: Verstappen beats Hamilton to pole in Malaysia

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen claimed Red Bull's first pole position of the season as he beat Lewis Hamilton in qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.
metadata.content: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen beats Lewis Hamilton to pole position to claim first Red Bull pole of 2026 Formula 1 season | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen beats Lewis Hamilton to pole position to claim first Red Bull pole of 2026 Formula 1 season Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together for the first time in over three years; George Russell will be in seventh after poor qualifying; watch the Bahrain GP in Malaysia at 8am with build-up from 6.30am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event By Nigel Chiu in Sepang Saturday 3 October 2026 18:04, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of qualifying at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia on the Sepang International Circuit Max Verstappen claimed Red Bull's first pole position of the season as he beat Lewis Hamilton in qualifying for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. Verstappen and Hamilton will share the front row in Sunday's race at 8am (build-up from 6.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event, for the first time since Hungary 2023 after the Red Bull driver delivered a dominant qualifying performance. The Dutchman topped each segment of qualifying and set two laps good enough for pole, ending up 0.298s faster than Hamilton who will target a second Ferrari win of the season.
